name: Forza Horizon 2 (Azimuth)
notes:
Azimuth (almost-there-games.itch.io/azimuth, v0.9.9) is a WRAPPER, not a port: it translates Xbox WinRT calls to Win32 and Xbox D3D11 to desktop D3D12, so the Xbox One build of Forza Horizon 2 runs on a PC. The game never had a PC release. Staged 2026-10-14.

PROTON, NOT NATIVE, AND THAT IS THE SUPPORTED PATH. There is no Linux build; the author lists Windows 10/11 and "Linux through Proton" as the targets and names handheld play as in scope. The binary is x86-64 and references d3d12/d3d11/dxgi/vkd3d/D3DCompiler, so vkd3d-proton does the heavy lifting — a better-placed stack for this AMD handheld than PinyonShift, which targets Vulkan directly and whose docs only qualify NVIDIA. Proton EXPERIMENTAL specifically, per the author.

It carries its own VS2012 runtime (msvcp110/msvcr110 in data/bin), so no vcrun install in the prefix.

THE GATE IS THE GAME EXE'S SHA-256, AND 1.0.0.64 IS HOW YOU GET THE RIGHT ONE. azimuth.exe carries 103 distinct pinned 64-hex hashes and the strings "Game executable hash mismatch" and "Not a folder of a supported game" (both confirmed present in the binary). So the version number is necessary but not sufficient — a differently packaged or re-dumped 1.0.0.64 can still be refused, and the symptom is a hash mismatch rather than anything about the version. The pinned set is also why this recipe can never be generalised to another game: a new title needs a record only the developer can add. Verified from the dump's own Mount/AppxManifest.xml: Identity Name="Anthem" Version="1.0.0.64", DisplayName "Forza Horizon 2", TitleId 1A96545B, Executable Forza_Durango_Release_Final.exe. "Anthem" is FH2's internal package name — the map geometry lives under Mount/media/tracks/anthem/ — so a folder called Anthem_1.0.0.64_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe IS Forza Horizon 2 and is not mislabelled.

LAYOUT MATTERS AND THE EXE SAYS SO. The package folder must be whole: era.vbi + Mount/ + EmbeddedXvd/, all three. EmbeddedXvd is not padding — it holds EmbeddedXvd/Windows/System32/xg_x.dll, the Xbox graphics-tiling library the D3D11.X-to-D3D12 translation needs for placement and XG tiled textures (confirmed present on the staged copy). The game exe inside is Mount/forza_durango_release_final.exe, 55.5 MB — note it is LOWERCASE on disk while AppxManifest.xml declares it mixed-case. On btrfs that is a different path, so never retype it from the manifest; this is the Halo MCC wrong-case bug waiting to happen again. Azimuth refuses anything else with "Not a game folder or a content package: no Mount\AppxManifest.xml", and warns "(copy the whole package folder, not only Mount)". Its own data/ folder must sit beside azimuth.exe or it reports "Azimuth's data folder is missing or incomplete".

WHY THIS TRAVELS. data/azimuth.ini records the game under [title-1a96545b] as folder=Anthem_1.0.0.64_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe — a RELATIVE folder name, no absolute path anywhere in the file. So the staged tree can move between machines unchanged, the same property that makes PinyonShift portable. The exe also accepts --game=DIR for scripted runs, which is the fallback if the ini is ever lost; it is not needed while the ini is intact, and the launcher would be skipped.

Offline only: no Xbox Live, so no multiplayer, clubs or achievements. 0.9.9 pre-release with frequent fixes. There is no in-game quit — exit with the Steam button.

TWO SEPARATE PIPELINE CACHES, and only one is disposable. Do not conflate them. (a) data/bin/azimuth.pipelines, 2.4 MB, format AZMPIPE1, SHIPPED by the author and keyed per game-exe hash — this one is part of the payload, keep it. (b) data/cache/pipelines-<vendor>-<device>-....bin, 87.4 MB, GENERATED and keyed by GPU; the staged one is 10de/2684, an NVIDIA desktop card, so it is dead weight on this AMD handheld and RADV will build its own on first run. Harmless, left in place rather than special-cased. data/cache/translated-*.pack (49.1 MB) is keyed by game, not GPU, so that one should carry over.

The staged azimuth.ini is tuned for the desktop: frame_rate=165, hdr=on, msaax4, resolution=1080. Worth turning down on the handheld — the author reports 720p60 or 1080p30 on a Steam Deck, and the Legion Go 2 is comfortably faster than a Deck, so 1080p60 is a reasonable target rather than a guarantee.

save_paths are NOT verified. Nothing had been saved at staging time, so there was nothing to confirm against. data/titles/1A96545B is the per-title state directory (title id from the manifest) and is the obvious candidate; azimuth.ini is listed alongside it because the graphics configuration is worth keeping even though it is settings rather than a save. If a capture of this recipe comes back empty, that path is wrong — which is the only symptom you get.
post_apply_message: Forza Horizon 2 (Azimuth) added to Steam on Proton Experimental. On first launch point the launcher at the folder holding Mount if it asks — it should already be remembered, since azimuth.ini stores it relatively. Turn the settings down from the desktop defaults (165fps/HDR) before playing on the handheld. No in-game quit: use the Steam button.
